column1: UC-001,UC-001 — Team member writes traceable items in AsciiDoc,use_case,,self-traceability/use-cases.adoc,""".Use Case: Team member writes traceable items in AsciiDoc

column3: Team member writes traceable items in AsciiDoc
Team member writes traceable items so that the project establishes complete end-to-end traceability across the software development lifecycle
Business Analyst, Architect, Developer, Test Manager — any team member who authors traceable content

The project uses Antora as its site generator And the Antora Tracer extension is installed in the playbook And a `traceability.yml` config is loaded with at least one role defined And the team member has write access to `.adoc` files in the pages or partials directories
Team member opens an `.adoc` file in their editor to add or update a traceable item

column1: . Team member identifies a concept that needs to be traceable — a requirement, a design decision, a test specification, or a dependency
. Team member determines the next available ID for the item's prefix using the CLI: `antora-tracer next-id --prefix <PREFIX> -i <path>`
. Team member assigns the concept to a role defined in the project's traceability domain model (requirement, design, test, etc.)
. Team member writes the item using the `[#ID, item, role=...]` block macro with a description between `--` delimiters
. Team member links the concept to related items already in the traceability graph using inline relationship macros (e.g., `addresses:REQ-001[]`)
. Team member includes rendering macros (`traceability:links[]`, `traceability:outgoing[]`, `traceability:incoming[]`) to display relationship lists in the rendered output
. Team member commits the file And triggers an Antora build
. The extension registers the item in the traceability graph And its relationships appear in the traceability matrix
. *No existing items share the prefix:* The `next-id` command defaults to 3-digit padding and returns `<PREFIX>-001`.
. *Team member uses a role not in config:* Extension registers the item with a warning. Processing continues.
. *Team member links to a target that does not exist:* Extension stores the relationship with a warning. The matrix shows a partial link.
. *Team member writes an incomplete item block:* The item may not register correctly in the traceability graph.
. *Team member includes rendering macros but no relationships exist:* The placeholder is replaced with an empty section in the rendered output.

column3: The traceability graph contains the new item with a consistent ID And all inline relationships are registered And the rendered page shows relationship lists if macros were included And the traceability matrix reflects updated coverage
High
Per item — multiple times per documentation session
The `[item]` macro syntax is documented in the User Guide — this use case describes the workflow, not the exact syntax. The `next-id` command auto-detects padding from existing IDs.

column1: UC-002,UC-002 — Requirements Engineer defines custom domain model via config,use_case,,self-traceability/use-cases.adoc,""".Use Case: Requirements Engineer defines custom domain model via config

column3: Requirements Engineer defines custom domain model via config
Requirements Engineer defines custom roles, relations, and matrices so that the project's traceability reflects its specific domain language rather than a generic template
Requirements Engineer

The Antora Tracer extension is installed And a built-in preset exists that covers the baseline domain (e.g., `requirements-engineering`) And the Requirements Engineer has write access to the project's `traceability.yml` file
Requirements Engineer determines that the built-in preset does not fully capture the project's domain — a missing role, an unneeded relation, or a custom matrix is needed

column1: . Requirements Engineer reviews the available built-in presets to identify the closest match
. Requirements Engineer creates a `traceability.yml` file with `extends:` pointing to the chosen preset
. Requirements Engineer adds roles not present in the preset (e.g., `use_case`, `stakeholder`)
. Requirements Engineer defines relations for the new roles (e.g., `use_case → requirement: [leads_to]`)
. Requirements Engineer adds custom matrices for the new role combinations
. Requirements Engineer runs the Antora build to verify the extended config is valid
. The extension merges the user config with the preset And items using the new roles are accepted
. *Requirements Engineer extends a preset that does not exist:* Extension reports an error listing available presets.
. *Requirements Engineer adds a role already in the preset:* The duplicate is silently merged — the preset's definition takes precedence.
. *Requirements Engineer defines a relation not allowed by the preset:* The extension warns but does not block processing. Items using the relation may fail validation.
. *Requirements Engineer does not include `extends:` field:* The config is treated as standalone — the preset is not loaded.

column3: The project's traceability domain model is configured And items using the new roles are accepted by the extension And custom matrices appear in the traceability output
High
Once per project — updated infrequently as the domain model evolves
⚠ Actor """"Requirements Engineer"""" does not yet have a persona definition. The `extends:` mechanism is documented in the User Guide (Configuration section).

column1: UC-004,UC-004 — Requirements Engineer organizes items in partial files,use_case,,self-traceability/use-cases.adoc,""".Use Case: Requirements Engineer organizes items in partial files

column3: Requirements Engineer organizes items in partial files
Requirements Engineer places related items in separate partial files so that the traceability structure stays modular, focused, and maintainable without cluttering the main page
Requirements Engineer

The project uses Antora as its site generator And the Antora Tracer extension is installed And the project has a `partials/` directory in its Antora module And the Requirements Engineer has write access to both page and partial files
Requirements Engineer notices that a page contains many item blocks or that a group of related items would benefit from being in a standalone file

column1: . Requirements Engineer creates a `.adoc` file in the `partials/` directory
. Requirements Engineer moves related `[item]` blocks from a page into the partial file
. Requirements Engineer replaces the moved items in the page with `include::partial$...[]` directives
. Requirements Engineer commits the changes And triggers an Antora build
. The extension processes both the page and the partial — items from the partial are registered in the graph And matrix links point to the partial's source location in the repository
. *Requirements Engineer includes a partial that defines no items:* The partial is included normally in the page output but contributes nothing to the traceability graph.
. *Requirements Engineer includes a partial in multiple pages:* The build fails with a duplicate-ID error naming both definitions.

. *Requirements Engineer references a partial item with `xref:`:* Asciidoctor reports """"target of xref not found"""" — partials do not produce HTML pages. Use inline relationship macros or `link:` URLs instead.

column3: The traceability graph contains the items from the partial And matrix links point to the partial's source file in the repository And the page content is rendered with the partial included
Medium
During initial documentation setup and periodically as the item count grows
⚠ Actor """"Requirements Engineer"""" does not yet have a persona definition. The partial processing behavior is documented in the User Guide section """"Items in Partials"""".

column1: UC-005,UC-005 — Reviewer browses traceability matrices for coverage,use_case,,self-traceability/use-cases.adoc,""".Use Case: Reviewer browses traceability matrices for coverage

column3: Reviewer browses traceability matrices for coverage
Reviewer inspects traceability matrices so that they can verify which requirements are covered by design decisions, tests, and other downstream artifacts
Reviewer or Auditor

The Antora site has been built And traceability matrices have been registered in the content catalog during the `contentClassified` event And the site navigation includes links to the matrix pages And the Reviewer has access to the published site
Reviewer needs to verify coverage — during a design review, a compliance audit, or a quality gate

column1: . Reviewer opens the published Antora site in a browser
. Reviewer navigates to the Traceability section in the navigation
. Reviewer opens the relevant matrix (e.g., Requirements → Architecture, Requirements → Tests, Use Cases → Requirements)
. Reviewer scans rows to identify items with missing coverage (red """"missing"""" badge, 0.0%)
. Reviewer clicks on cell items to navigate to the source page where the relationship is defined
. Reviewer clicks on row items to navigate to the requirement's definition
. Reviewer notes gaps And either approves the coverage or requests additions
. *A matrix shows no items:* The corresponding roles have no items defined. The matrix renders with zero rows.
. *A row shows partial coverage (yellow):* Some but not all expected relationships exist. Reviewer investigates the specific gap.
. *Reviewer needs to see the source data in CSV:* Reviewer can open the `.csv` variant of the matrix for offline analysis.
. *Reviewer needs coverage data for external tools:* Reviewer can export the graph to Neo4j CSV or Cypher format for import into graph databases or compliance reports.

column3: Reviewer has assessed coverage completeness And identified any gaps And can navigate from the matrix to the source items for further investigation
High
Periodically — at design reviews, before releases, during compliance audits

⚠ Actor """"Reviewer or Auditor"""" — two distinct roles with similar workflows. Consider splitting if their goals diverge significantly (internal review vs. external compliance). No persona defined for either.

column1: UC-006,UC-006 — Project lead bootstraps traceability for a new project,use_case,,self-traceability/use-cases.adoc,""".Use Case: Project lead bootstraps traceability for a new project

column3: Project lead bootstraps traceability for a new project
Project lead sets up the Antora Tracer extension for a new or existing Antora project so the team can begin writing traceable items with a domain model appropriate to their workflow
Project Lead, Requirements Engineer, or Tech Lead
The project uses Antora as its site generator And the project lead has access to the Antora playbook and module directories
The team decides to adopt traceability — a new project is starting, or an existing project wants to add traceability to its documentation

column1: . Project lead installs the extension: `npm install antora-tracer --save-dev`
. Project lead reviews the built-in presets to find the closest match for the team's domain (requirements-engineering, agile, medical-iec62304, minimal)
. Project lead adds the extension to the Antora playbook with the chosen preset:
. Project lead creates a `traceability.yml` file extending the preset with any project-specific roles, relations, or matrices
. Project lead adds `:traceability-links:` document attributes to the pages where relationship macros should render
. Project lead adds matrix links to the site navigation (e.g., `xref:attachment$traceability/matrix-requirements-to-design.html[]`)
. Project lead runs a first Antora build to verify the extension initializes and matrices generate without errors
. Project lead shares the setup with the team — team members can now write items in their AsciiDoc pages
. *The preset does not cover the team's domain at all:* Project lead uses `preset init` to bootstrap a custom preset from scratch and defines all roles, relations, and matrices manually.
. *The project does not have a `partials/` directory yet:* Project lead creates one. The extension processes partials automatically.
. *The first build shows zero items in matrices:* Expected — the team has not written any items yet. Matrices render with empty rows and 0% coverage.
. *The team wants to adopt incrementally:* Project lead configures the extension with minimal roles first. Additional roles, relations, and matrices are added later via config extension.
. *The project uses multiple Antora components:* Project lead configures the extension in each component's playbook or uses a shared config.

column3: The Antora Tracer extension is installed and configured And at least one preset is active And the site navigation includes matrix links And matrices generate during builds with 0 errors And the team can begin writing traceable items
High
Once per project — revisited when the domain model evolves
This use case covers the """"Day 0"""" setup. For ongoing configuration changes, see UC-002. The `preset init` command creates a skeleton YAML file for a custom preset.

column1: UC-007,UC-007 — Developer validates traceability in CI pipeline,use_case,,self-traceability/use-cases.adoc,""".Use Case: Developer validates traceability in CI pipeline

column3: Developer validates traceability in CI pipeline
Developer runs traceability validation in CI so that invalid relationships, circular references, and configuration errors are caught before they reach the published site
Developer or DevOps Engineer

The Antora Tracer CLI is installed in the CI environment And the project's `.adoc` source files are checked out And a `traceability.yml` config is present And the CI pipeline has a step for traceability validation
A pull request is opened or a commit is pushed — the CI pipeline triggers a traceability validation job

column1: . CI pipeline checks out the repository
. CI pipeline runs `antora-tracer process -i <pages-dir> --config traceability.yml` to parse all items
. CI pipeline runs `antora-tracer validate -i <pages-dir> --config traceability.yml` to check graph integrity
. The validator reports errors (circular references, invalid relations) and warnings (unknown roles, missing targets)
. If errors are found, the CI pipeline fails the build and the developer reviews the output
. Developer fixes the issues — removes circular references, corrects relation types, or adds missing targets
. Developer pushes the fix And CI re-runs validation
. When validation passes (0 errors), the pipeline proceeds to build and deploy the Antora site
. *Validation finds only warnings (no errors):* The build continues. Warnings are logged for review but do not block deployment.
. *Circular reference detected (e.g., A → B → A):* The validator reports the full cycle path. Developer must break the cycle by removing one of the relationships.
. *Config file is missing or invalid:* The validator exits with an error describing the config problem. Developer fixes `traceability.yml`.
. *No items found in the input directory:* The validator reports 0 items. This may be intentional (new project) or indicate a path misconfiguration.
. *Developer wants to run validation locally before pushing:* Same commands work outside CI — `process` then `validate`.

column3: The traceability graph is free of structural errors (0 circular references, 0 invalid relations) And the CI pipeline has verified the config is valid And the build can proceed to site generation
High
On every push or pull request — continuous integration

The `process` step must run before `validate` — validation operates on the in-memory graph populated by processing. The CLI can also generate matrices (`matrix`) and export Neo4j data (`export neo4j`) in CI for artifact generation.

column1: UC-008,UC-008 — Data analyst explores traceability in Neo4j,use_case,,self-traceability/use-cases.adoc,""".Use Case: Data analyst explores traceability in Neo4j

column3: Data analyst explores traceability in Neo4j
Data analyst exports the traceability graph to Neo4j so they can run complex graph queries, generate compliance reports, and discover patterns not visible in the matrix views
Data Analyst, Compliance Officer, or Systems Engineer
The traceability graph has been populated with items and relationships And the Antora Tracer CLI is available And Neo4j is installed or accessible (Desktop, AuraDB, or Docker)

Data analyst needs to answer a question that requires graph traversal — """"show me all requirements with no test coverage,"""" """"trace the impact chain for this change,"""" or """"generate a compliance audit trail""""

column1: . Data analyst runs `antora-tracer export neo4j -i <pages-dir> --format csv` to generate `nodes.csv` and `relationships.csv`
. Data analyst imports the CSV files into Neo4j using `LOAD CSV` or the Neo4j Data Importer
. Data analyst runs preset queries included with the config (e.g., """"Uncovered Requirements,"""" """"Coverage Summary,"""" """"Traceability Chains"""")
. Data analyst writes custom Cypher queries for project-specific questions
. Data analyst shares findings — a coverage heatmap, a list of orphan items, or an impact analysis report
. *Data analyst prefers Cypher format:* Uses `--format cypher` to generate an `import.cypher` file with `CREATE` statements instead of CSV.
. *Export contains items with special characters in titles:* The exporter properly escapes commas, quotes, and newlines so CSV imports cleanly.
. *Data analyst wants to export only a subset:* Runs `export neo4j` after a CI validation step that has already populated the graph with only the items of interest.
. *Neo4j is not available:* The analyst can inspect the CSV files directly in a spreadsheet or use the Cypher file as documentation of the graph structure.

column3: The traceability graph is available in Neo4j And preset queries return results And the data analyst can run ad-hoc Cypher queries for deep analysis
Medium
Periodically — before releases, during audits, or when investigating coverage gaps

The `cypher` format includes `:Item` and role-specific labels on nodes, and type-specific labels on relationships. The `includeContent` option controls whether item body text is included in the export.

column1: UC-009,UC-009 — Architect visualizes relationship dependencies,use_case,,self-traceability/use-cases.adoc,""".Use Case: Architect visualizes relationship dependencies

column3: Architect visualizes relationship dependencies
Architect embeds relationship graphs and coverage charts in documentation pages so stakeholders can visually explore dependencies and coverage at a glance without leaving the documentation site
Architect, Tech Lead, or Requirements Engineer

The Antora Tracer extension is installed And the `:traceability-graph:` document attribute is enabled on the target pages And Kroki is configured in the Antora playbook (for rendering GraphViz and Vega-Lite)
Architect wants to provide visual context — showing how a key requirement connects to downstream artifacts, or displaying global coverage status on a dashboard page

column1: . Architect adds `:traceability-graph: true` to a page's document header
. Architect embeds `traceability:graph[]` inside an item block to render a GraphViz diagram of that item's direct relationships (colored by role, with labeled edges)
. Architect embeds `traceability:graph-coverage[]` inside or outside item blocks to render Vega-Lite bar charts showing coverage
. Architect builds the Antora site — macros are replaced with Kroki image URLs (SVG by default, PNG configurable)
. Stakeholders view the page — the diagram shows the item's dependency neighborhood and the bar chart shows coverage status
. Stakeholders can click through from the diagram description to related items via xrefs
. *Architect uses `traceability:graph[ITEM-ID, 2]` with a depth of 2:* The graph shows two hops of relationships instead of one.
. *Architect places `traceability:graph-coverage[]` outside an item block:* The chart shows global coverage by role instead of per-item coverage.
. *The project builds PDFs:* Architect sets `krokiImageFormat: png` in the playbook config — PNG images render correctly in PDF output where SVGs do not.
. *Kroki is unavailable or misconfigured:* The macros render as fallback text with the item IDs, still providing value.

column3: The documentation page contains embedded relationship graphs and/or coverage charts And stakeholders can visually explore dependencies And the graphs are navigable via xrefs to related items
Medium
Per key item — added to pages where visual context adds value (dashboard, architecture overview, key requirements)
The dashboard page (`dashboard.adoc`) demonstrates both macros in context. GraphViz diagrams are rendered server-side by Kroki; Vega-Lite is rendered client-side by the browser.

column1: UC-010,UC-010 — Developer assesses impact before changing a traceable item,use_case,,self-traceability/use-cases.adoc,""".Use Case: Developer assesses impact before changing a traceable item

column3: Developer assesses impact before changing a traceable item
Developer queries the traceability graph so they can identify every item that references a target before changing or removing it, avoiding dangling references and broken coverage
Developer or Requirements Engineer
The project's `.adoc` source files contain traceable items with IDs And the Antora Tracer CLI is available And the developer has read access to the source files
Developer plans to change, rename, or remove a traceable item and needs to know what references it

column1: . Developer identifies the ID of the item they intend to change or remove
. Developer runs `antora-tracer query reverse <ID>` to list every item that references the target, with relationship type and source file and line
. Developer runs `antora-tracer query impact <ID>` to list all items transitively connected to the target
. Developer reviews the results to determine the full set of items affected by the change
. Developer updates each referencing item — or confirms none exist — before making the change
. Developer commits the change with all affected items accounted for
. *No item references the target:* `reverse` returns an empty result and exits 0. The change is safe from a traceability perspective.
. *The target ID does not exist:* The command exits 1 with an """"Item not found"""" warning. Developer verifies the ID spelling or confirms the item was already removed.
. *Developer needs machine-readable output:* Developer adds `--json` for structured output consumable by scripts or AI coding agents.
. *Developer needs the chain between two specific items:* Developer runs `query path <from> <to>`. The shortest relationship path prints, or the command exits 1 with """"No path found"""".
. *Developer wants to find items with no relationships:* Developer runs `query orphaned`, optionally filtered with `--role`.
. *Developer wants to limit the search:* Developer passes `-i <path>` to scan a specific directory or file instead of the current directory.

column3: The developer has identified every item that references the target And no Antora build was required And no source files were modified (query is read-only) And the change can proceed with all referencing items accounted for
Medium
Before each refactor, rename, or removal of a traceable item

The `query` command parses `.adoc` files directly — it reuses the same parser and graph as the build, so no Antora build or running Neo4j database is required. This is the lightweight in-repo counterpart to UC-008 (Neo4j exploration): `query` answers simple structural questions without infrastructure, while Neo4j supports deeper ad-hoc graph analysis. ⚠ Actor """"Developer or Requirements Engineer"""" is a compound role without a persona definition.

column1: CON-001,CON-001 — Antora extension integration,constraint,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL be implemented as an Antora extension, integrating via the Antora extension API (`contentClassified` and `sitePublished` events).
No Antora build pipeline modification or custom Antora fork SHALL be required."""
CON-002,CON-002 — Source files are never modified,constraint,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL NOT modify any `.adoc` source file on disk at any point during processing.
All content transformations (macro expansion, link substitution, title injection) SHALL operate exclusively on in-memory content buffers."""

CON-003,CON-003 — Generated output uses standard AsciiDoc constructs,constraint,,requirements.adoc,"""All content generated by the extension's macros (relationship lists, link blocks, graphs) SHALL use standard AsciiDoc constructs only — not raw HTML.
This ensures compatibility with all Asciidoctor backends, including HTML and PDF."""
CON-004,CON-004 — Runtime is Node.js 20+ with ESM,constraint,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL run on Node.js 20 or later.
The package SHALL use ECMAScript modules (`""""type"""": """"module""""`) throughout.
No runtime framework SHALL be introduced as a dependency."""
CON-005,CON-005 — Document format is AsciiDoc processed by Antora,constraint,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL process AsciiDoc files as managed by Antora's content catalog.
Direct filesystem reads of source `.adoc` files SHALL only occur in the standalone CLI path, where no Antora content catalog is available."""

REQ-087,REQ-087 — Items inside verbatim blocks are not parsed,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL NOT register item declarations (`[#ID, item, role=...]`) found inside AsciiDoc verbatim blocks (listing blocks delimited by `----` and literal blocks delimited by `....`) as traceability items.

REQ-088,REQ-088 — Inline macros inside verbatim blocks are not parsed,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL NOT register inline relationship macros (`relation:TARGET[]`) whose enclosing item was skipped because it fell inside a verbatim block.

REQ-090,REQ-090 — Verbatim block detection handles standard AsciiDoc fences,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL detect verbatim blocks by matching opening and closing fence lines consisting of exactly `----` or `....` (with optional trailing whitespace), ignoring style prefix lines like `[source,asciidoc]`.

REQ-091,REQ-091 — Inline macros inside verbatim blocks are preserved in rendered output,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL NOT strip inline relationship macros (`relation:TARGET[]`) from inside AsciiDoc verbatim blocks during the content substitution pass.
Such macros are example code and SHALL remain visible in the rendered output.

REQ-092,REQ-092 — Inline macros inside backtick code spans are not parsed,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL NOT register inline relationship macros (`relation:ID[]`) that appear inside backtick-enclosed code spans as traceability relationships.

REQ-110,REQ-110 — Items defined in partials are registered in the graph,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL process items defined in AsciiDoc partial files alongside page files, registering them in the traceability graph.

REQ-144,REQ-144 — Partial items use view URL as source reference,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""Items from partial files SHALL use the file's view URL as their source file reference, enabling traceability matrix links to resolve to the source repository.

REQ-145,REQ-145 — All processing passes apply to partial files,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL apply graph population, macro expansion, and link substitution passes to partial files in the same way as page files, because partial content is inlined into pages and reaches the browser.

REQ-129,REQ-129 — Bidirectional relationship pairs are merged into a single edge,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL detect when a newly added relationship is authored with the reverse of an existing relationship's type — the existing edge goes from B to A with a type whose declared `reverse` equals the new edge's type — and SHALL NOT store a second edge.
The canonical primary edge is retained with its original metadata (sourceFile, line), and no warning is emitted.
Merging is driven by the `reverse` declaration in `relations` (config), not by `inverseLabels` or the compile-time `INVERSE_MAP`.
REQ-109,REQ-109 — Circular reference detection in graph validation,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL detect circular references in the traceability graph during validation.
A circular reference is a cycle in the directed relationship graph (e.g., A → B → A, or A → B → C → A).
Self-referencing relationships (A → A) SHALL also be detected as cycles.
Auto-generated inverse relationships SHALL be skipped during cycle detection to avoid false positives.
Relationships marked as bidirectional SHALL also be skipped during cycle detection.

REQ-111,REQ-111 — File state is prepared once per file,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL compute file content, document attributes, and item block positions exactly once per page file, and SHALL reuse the computed values across all macro-expansion passes for that file.

REQ-112,REQ-112 — PreparedFile carries all needed state,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL cache the parsed state of each source file — including its full content, document attributes, item block positions, and normalized source-file metadata — so that subsequent processing steps within the same file pass do not reparse it.

REQ-044,REQ-044 — traceability:outgoing[] macro renders outgoing links,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL provide a `traceability:outgoing[]` macro that expands to a formatted list of all outgoing relationships for the enclosing item.

REQ-146,REQ-146 — Empty-state message when item has no outgoing relationships,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""If the enclosing item has no outgoing relationships, then the `traceability:outgoing[]` macro SHALL render a configurable empty-state message controlled by the `:traceability-empty:` document attribute.

REQ-055,REQ-055 — traceability:incoming[] macro renders incoming links,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL provide a `traceability:incoming[]` macro that expands to a formatted list of all relationships pointing to the enclosing item (reverse relationships).

REQ-104,REQ-104 — traceability:links[] macro renders combined outgoing and incoming links,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL provide a `traceability:links[]` macro that expands to a combined list of all outgoing and incoming relationships for the enclosing item, with outgoing groups rendered first followed by incoming groups.

REQ-045,REQ-045 — Opt-in via AsciiDoc attribute,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL only expand `traceability:outgoing[]` and `traceability:incoming[]` when the `:traceability-links:` document attribute is set to a truthy value.

REQ-100,REQ-100 — Inline macros suppressed when links macros are active,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""When `:traceability-links:` is enabled, the system SHALL suppress the individual rendering of inline relationship macros within item blocks that contain a `traceability:outgoing[]` or `traceability:incoming[]` macro.

REQ-047,REQ-047 — Configurable display style,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL support configurable display styles via the `:traceability-style:` document attribute for both `traceability:outgoing[]` and `traceability:incoming[]` macros.

REQ-048,REQ-048 — Configurable sort order,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL support configurable sort order via the `:traceability-order:` document attribute for both `traceability:outgoing[]` and `traceability:incoming[]` macros, defaulting to sort by target ID for outgoing and source ID for incoming.

REQ-102,REQ-102 — Collapsible list-style output via document attribute,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL support a `:traceability-collapsible:` document attribute that, when set to a truthy value, wraps each relation-type group in list-style output in a `[%collapsible]` AsciiDoc block.

REQ-064,REQ-064 — Incoming macro respects document attributes,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL gate `traceability:incoming[]` expansion on the same `:traceability-links:` document attribute as the outgoing macro.

REQ-065,REQ-065 — Incoming macro display styles,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL support the same display styles for `traceability:incoming[]` as for the outgoing macro, via the `:traceability-style:` document attribute.

REQ-066,REQ-066 — Incoming macro sort order,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL support the same sort orders for `traceability:incoming[]` as for the outgoing macro, via the `:traceability-order:` document attribute, defaulting to sort by source ID.

REQ-067,REQ-067 — Incoming groups use the reverse relation type,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL group incoming relationships in `traceability:incoming[]` by the reverse relation type — the declared `reverse` of the relationship's type — so each group heading names the relation from the target item's perspective.

REQ-070,REQ-070 — Incoming macro supports collapsible output,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL apply the same `:traceability-collapsible:` document attribute to `traceability:incoming[]` output as it does for `traceability:outgoing[]`.
When enabled, each inverse relation-type group in list-style incoming output SHALL be wrapped in a `[%collapsible]` block.

REQ-103,REQ-103 — Graph isolation per component version,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""When building a site with multiple component versions, relationship macro expansion SHALL be scoped per version.
Items from one component version SHALL NOT appear in xrefs generated for pages in a different component version.

REQ-163,REQ-163 — Incoming macro PDF compatibility,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The generated output from `traceability:incoming[]` SHALL be standard AsciiDoc constructs — not raw HTML — ensuring compatibility with both HTML and PDF backends.
REQ-164,REQ-164 — Source file not modified by incoming macro,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL NOT modify the `.adoc` source file on disk when expanding `traceability:incoming[]`.

REQ-165,REQ-165 — PDF compatibility,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The generated output from `traceability:outgoing[]` and `traceability:incoming[]` SHALL use standard AsciiDoc constructs, ensuring compatibility with both HTML and PDF rendering backends.

REQ-166,REQ-166 — Source file not modified,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL NOT modify the `.adoc` source file on disk when expanding `traceability:outgoing[]` or `traceability:incoming[]`.

REQ-116,REQ-116 — Items carry component and module context from Antora,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""When processing `.adoc` files through the Antora extension, the system SHALL store the Antora component and module names on each `Item` so that downstream xref and link generation can distinguish same-module from cross-module and cross-component references.

REQ-117,REQ-117 — Cross-module and cross-component xref includes correct prefix,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""When `buildXref` generates an Antora xref for an item in a different module or component than the current page, the system SHALL include the appropriate prefix matching Antora's xref resolution hierarchy: `component:module:` for cross-component, `module:` for cross-module, and no prefix for same-module.

REQ-119,REQ-119 — Cross-module and cross-component xref resolution,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""When an item in one module has relationships to items in other modules or components, the `traceability:outgoing[]` and `traceability:incoming[]` macros SHALL generate xrefs with the correct Antora prefix (`component:module:` or `module:`) so Antora can resolve them correctly.

REQ-071,REQ-071 — Relation display names are config-driven,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL support `labels` in the traceability configuration YAML, mapping each relation type to a human-readable display name used for rendering (incoming/outgoing lists, matrix headers, graph labels).
`labels` SHALL NOT affect graph structure, merge behavior, or validation.

REQ-161,REQ-161 — Default display name is the humanized type,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""If a relation type has no entry in `labels`, the system SHALL display the type name humanized: underscores replaced with spaces and the result sentence-cased.

REQ-162,REQ-162 — No compile-time fallback,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL NOT consult a compile-time inverse map for display names; the pairing between primary and reverse types is derived solely from the `reverse` declaration in `relations`, and display text comes solely from `labels` or the humanized default.

REQ-037,REQ-037 — Matrix displays row items as clickable links,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The matrix SHALL render row item IDs as hyperlinks that navigate to the item's definition in the rendered HTML documentation.

REQ-038,REQ-038 — Matrix displays cell items as clickable links,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The matrix SHALL render cell item IDs as hyperlinks that navigate to the item's definition in the rendered HTML documentation.
REQ-039,REQ-039 — Links include source file tooltip,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The matrix SHALL display the source file name as a tooltip when users hover over item links.

REQ-040,REQ-040 — Matrix links resolve correctly from site output location,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL generate matrix links that resolve correctly regardless of where the matrix file is served within the Antora site output.

REQ-041,REQ-041 — Source file paths are normalized,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL normalize item source file references so that matrix links resolve to the rendered page URL rather than the AsciiDoc source file path.

REQ-042,REQ-042 — Matrix renders correctly without link resolution configured,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL maintain existing matrix rendering behaviour when link resolution is not configured.
REQ-043,REQ-043 — Non-HTML matrix outputs unchanged,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL NOT modify CSV and JSON matrix outputs to include links.

REQ-128,REQ-128 — Matrix links include module path for module-aware items,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""When an item has module information, the system SHALL generate HTML links that include the module name so the link navigates to the correct module page.

REQ-108,REQ-108 — Matrix files registered in the content catalog,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL register generated matrix files (HTML, CSV, JSON) as site attachments before document conversion, so that `attachment$traceability/...` xrefs in pages and navigation resolve correctly.
Registration SHALL occur per component version and under every module that has AsciiDoc content.
A committed copy, if present, SHALL have its contents refreshed in place.

REQ-130,REQ-130 — Matrix links are compatible with Antora indexify URL style,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""When Antora's `indexify` URL style is active (root-level pages are served as `pagename/index.html`), the system SHALL generate matrix links that include `index.html` in the path for root-level pages so links from traceability matrices resolve to the correct page.

REQ-113,REQ-113 — Matrix template uses partials for structure,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The HTML matrix template SHALL be split into a main template and four reusable partial fragments (`styles`, `header`, `matrix-row`, `footer`) loaded from the `partials/` subdirectory.

REQ-167,REQ-167 — Matrix renders one status column per row,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The HTML matrix SHALL render exactly one per-row status column, and SHALL NOT render a separate per-row coverage percentage column.

REQ-168,REQ-168 — Coverage summary remains,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The matrix SHALL still render a top-level coverage summary with the counts of done/partial/missing rows and an overall percentage of done rows.
REQ-169,REQ-169 — CSV output is unchanged,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The CSV export SHALL NOT render a per-row status or coverage column, matching its current behavior.

REQ-083,REQ-083 — Preset defines pairwise requirements-to-design matrix,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The `requirements-engineering` preset SHALL include a matrix named `requirements-to-design` with `requirement` rows and a single `design` column.

REQ-084,REQ-084 — Preset defines pairwise design-to-implementation matrix,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The `requirements-engineering` preset SHALL include a matrix named `design-to-implementation` with `design` rows and a single `implementation` column.

REQ-085,REQ-085 — Preset defines pairwise requirements-to-tests matrix,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The `requirements-engineering` preset SHALL include a matrix named `requirements-to-tests` with `requirement` rows and a single `test` column.
REQ-086,REQ-086 — Preset does not define wide multi-column matrices,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The `requirements-engineering` preset SHALL NOT define matrices with more than one column role.

REQ-170,REQ-170 — Preset extends a parent by top-level `extends`,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""A preset SHALL declare its parent with a top-level `extends` field (sibling of `name`, `version`, `description`).
When a preset declares `extends`, the resolved preset SHALL include the parent's `traceability` deep-merged under the child's own `traceability`.

REQ-171,REQ-171 — Merge semantics match config-file `extends`,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""Preset inheritance SHALL use the same merge rules as a config file extending a preset: roles are unioned, relations are deep-merged by source and target role, matrices are overridden by `name`, and `labels` are overridden key-by-key.

REQ-172,REQ-172 — Transitive inheritance,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""Inheritance SHALL resolve transitively: a preset extending a preset that itself extends another SHALL include the roles, relations, and matrices of the full chain.

REQ-173,REQ-173 — Missing parent is reported,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""When a preset's `extends` names a preset that cannot be resolved, loading SHALL fail with an error that names the missing preset.
REQ-174,REQ-174 — Circular inheritance is rejected,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""A preset SHALL NOT extend itself, directly or transitively.
Any inheritance cycle SHALL be detected and rejected with a clear error rather than looping indefinitely.

REQ-175,REQ-175 — Relations are declared keyed with a mandatory reverse,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The `relations` config SHALL map `sourceRole → targetRole → relationType → { reverse }`, where `reverse` is required and names the authorable reverse relation type.

REQ-176,REQ-176 — Authoring the reverse name canonicalizes to the primary edge,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""When an item authors a relationship using a reverse type, the graph SHALL store the canonical primary edge (primary direction and primary type), not the reverse-authored form.

REQ-177,REQ-177 — Reverse direction is derived for validation,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""`isRelationAllowed` SHALL allow a relation type that is the reverse of a relation declared in the opposite role direction, without an explicit `relations` entry for that direction.

REQ-178,REQ-178 — Matrix coverage matches the canonical primary type,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""A matrix `coverageRelations` entry SHALL name the canonical primary type, and a single entry SHALL count a relationship regardless of which name was authored.

REQ-051,REQ-051 — Relationship graph via traceability:graph[] macro,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL provide a `traceability:graph[]` inline macro that renders a relationship diagram for the enclosing item.
The diagram SHALL show the item and its related items as labeled nodes and edges, colored by role.
An optional depth parameter SHALL control the number of relationship hops shown.

REQ-052,REQ-052 — Coverage chart via traceability:graph-coverage[] macro,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL provide a `traceability:graph-coverage[]` inline macro that renders a coverage chart.
When used inside an item block, it SHALL show per-relationship-type coverage for that item.
When used outside an item block, it SHALL show global coverage by role.

REQ-053,REQ-053 — Graph model supports traversal-bounded subgraph and coverage queries,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The graph model SHALL support producing a traversal-bounded relationship subgraph for a given item, traversing both outgoing and incoming directions.
Bidirectional relationships SHALL be visually distinguishable from one-directional relationships in the rendered output.
The graph model SHALL also support producing coverage data for a given item, or globally across all items.

REQ-054,REQ-054 — Dashboard page in example site,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The example site SHALL include a dashboard page with a global coverage chart and select per-item relationship graphs, gated by the `:traceability-graph:` attribute.

REQ-063,REQ-063 — Configurable Kroki image format,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The `krokiImageFormat` extension config option SHALL control the image format (`svg` or `png`) used in rendered relationship diagram images.
When not set, the format SHALL default to `svg`.
The configured `krokiServerUrl` (or its default `https://kroki.io`) SHALL be used as the base URL for diagram rendering requests.

REQ-159,REQ-159 — Configuration graph via traceability:config-graph[] macro,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL provide a `traceability:config-graph[]` macro that renders the effective traceability configuration as a Kroki GraphViz diagram.
The diagram SHALL show each configured role as a node colored by role and each declared relation as a labeled edge, using declared directions only.

REQ-160,REQ-160 — Config graph generator renders configuration as DOT,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL provide a DOT generator for the traceability configuration that renders roles as nodes and declared relations as labeled edges.

REQ-142,REQ-142 — Configurable Kroki server URL via extension config,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The `krokiServerUrl` extension config option SHALL set the base URL used by `traceability:graph[]` and `traceability:graph-coverage[]` macros when generating Kroki image URLs.
When set, the system SHALL use this URL instead of the default `https://kroki.io`.
REQ-143,REQ-143 — Kroki server URL via environment variable,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The `KROKI_SERVER_URL` environment variable SHALL override the `krokiServerUrl` extension config option.
When set, the system SHALL use its value as the Kroki server base URL.

REQ-056,REQ-056 — CLI next-id command returns next available ID,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The CLI SHALL provide a `next-id` command that accepts a `--prefix` and `-i/--input` and returns the next available sequential ID for items matching that prefix.

REQ-136,REQ-136 — CLI exposes a query subcommand,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The CLI SHALL provide a `query` subcommand that reads AsciiDoc source files and answers one structural question about items and their relationships per invocation.
No Antora build SHALL be required.

REQ-137,REQ-137 — query reverse — find all items that point at a given ID,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The CLI SHALL provide `query reverse <id>` that returns all items whose relationship macros reference the given item ID.

REQ-138,REQ-138 — query impact — find all items connected to a given ID,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The CLI SHALL provide `query impact <id>` that returns all items transitively connected to the given item (its connected component, excluding the item itself), following relationships in both directions.

REQ-139,REQ-139 — query orphaned — find items with no relationships,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The CLI SHALL provide `query orphaned` that returns all items that have neither incoming nor outgoing relationships in the graph.

REQ-140,REQ-140 — query path — find the shortest path between two items,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The CLI SHALL provide `query path <from-id> <to-id>` that returns the shortest relationship path between two items in the graph.
REQ-141,REQ-141 — JSON output flag,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""All `query` subcommands SHALL accept a `--json` flag that switches output to a machine-readable JSON array.

REQ-150,REQ-150 — CLI exposes a validate command,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The CLI SHALL provide a `validate` command that reads AsciiDoc source files and reports validation errors — invalid relation types, orphaned relationships, duplicate item IDs, and circular references — with diagnostics naming the source and target item IDs with roles, the invalid relation type, and the allowed alternatives.
No Antora build SHALL be required.
The command SHALL exit with a non-zero code when errors are found and code 0 when the input is valid.

REQ-079,REQ-079 — Non-heading elements with IDs are indexed as navigable anchors,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The search index SHALL include every non-heading HTML element inside `<article class=""""doc"""">` that has an `id` attribute as a separate searchable chunk.
Each chunk SHALL use the element's `id` as its `hash`, enabling search result links to navigate directly to the element's anchor.

REQ-080,REQ-080 — Item title is extracted from `.title` child element,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""When an element has a child element with CSS class `title`, the extension SHALL use the text content of that child as the chunk's `title` field.
If no `.title` child exists, the element's `id` SHALL be used as the title.

REQ-081,REQ-081 — Heading elements are excluded from item indexing,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""Elements that are HTML headings (`h1` through `h6`) SHALL be skipped by the item anchor indexing pass, as they are already indexed by the existing heading-based section chunking.
REQ-082,REQ-082 — Item indexing is scoped to article body,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The item anchor indexing SHALL only traverse elements within `<article class=""""doc"""">`.
Elements outside the article body (navigation, TOC, footer) SHALL NOT be indexed.

REQ-201,REQ-201 — A successor declares a supersedes relationship,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""When a traceable item replaces another item, the successor SHALL declare a `supersedes` relationship to the predecessor.

REQ-202,REQ-202 — The reverse superseded_by relationship is derivable,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""When a successor declares a `supersedes` relationship, the predecessor's `superseded_by` relationship SHALL be derivable from the graph.

REQ-203,REQ-203 — Superseded state is derived from relationships,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""An item SHALL be effectively superseded when at least one valid incoming `supersedes` relationship targets it.

REQ-204,REQ-204 — Invalid supersession structures are rejected,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""If the supersession graph contains a self-reference, duplicate relationship, or cycle, then validation SHALL report an error.

REQ-205,REQ-205 — Current-state matrices omit superseded items,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""When a current-state matrix is generated, the system SHALL omit effectively superseded items from both rows and columns by default.

REQ-206,REQ-206 — Functional links to superseded items remain visible,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""When a relationship macro renders a functional relationship targeting a superseded item, the system SHALL retain the relationship and identify it as requiring review, naming every direct successor.
REQ-207,REQ-207 — History links are excluded from review worklists,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""Supersession history relationships SHALL NOT be classified as stale functional links.

REQ-208,REQ-208 — Superseded item blocks link to successors,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""When a superseded item's source block is rendered, the system SHALL display a superseded marker that links to every direct successor.

REQ-209,REQ-209 — CLI reports supersession impact,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""When a supersession check is requested, the CLI SHALL report direct successors and incoming functional relationships requiring review.
REQ-210,REQ-210 — Supersession checks do not modify source files,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""When a supersession check is requested, the CLI SHALL NOT modify any source file.

REQ-211,REQ-211 — Validation warns about stale functional links,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""When a functional relationship targets an effectively superseded item, validation SHALL emit a non-blocking warning naming the source item, relation type, predecessor, and all direct successors.

REQ-212,REQ-212 — Diff classifies items by stable ID,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""When two graph snapshots are compared, the diff SHALL classify each item as added, removed, or modified based on its stable ID.

REQ-213,REQ-213 — Modified items report changed fields,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""A surviving item SHALL be reported as modified when its `title`, `content`, `role`, `status`, or `attributes` differs between the snapshots, and the delta SHALL name the changed fields.
REQ-214,REQ-214 — Relationship deltas are limited to surviving items,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The diff SHALL report relationship changes only between items that exist in both snapshots.
REQ-215,REQ-215 — Supersession appears as added and removed,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The diff SHALL NOT attempt content-similarity rename detection.
A superseded predecessor SHALL appear as removed and its successor as added, with the `supersedes` relationship reported as a new relationship.

REQ-216,"""REQ-216 — Diff is a public, config-agnostic API""",requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The diff SHALL be exposed as a public function usable with any configured role or relation vocabulary, without hardcoding any role name.
REQ-217,REQ-217 — CLI diff is read-only,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""A `diff` CLI command SHALL scan two source paths, build two graphs, and print the delta without modifying any source file.
QA-058,QA-058 — No side effects on source files,requirement,,requirements.adoc,include::ROOT:partial$quality/qa-no-side-effects.adoc[]

REQ-093,REQ-093 — Devbox provides Ruby and Node.js for PDF builds,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The devbox.json configuration SHALL include `ruby`, `bundler`, and `nodejs` packages so that `devbox shell` provides a complete PDF build environment.
The init hook SHALL run `npm install` and `bundle install` automatically.

REQ-094,REQ-094 — Gemfile locks asciidoctor-pdf version,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The project SHALL include a `Gemfile` that specifies `asciidoctor-pdf` and `asciidoctor-kroki` gems so the PDF converter and diagram renderer are installed consistently across environments.

REQ-095,REQ-095 — PDF playbook generates PDF from example site,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""A separate `antora-playbook-pdf.yml` SHALL exist that uses `@antora/pdf-extension` to generate a single PDF from the example site's content.
The playbook SHALL use the same content sources as the HTML playbook but output to `public/pdf/`.

REQ-096,REQ-096 — PDF extension is a peer dependency,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The `@antora/pdf-extension` npm package SHALL be listed as a `peerDependency` (with `optional: true` in `peerDependenciesMeta`) so consumers who want PDF output are signalled to install it explicitly.
It SHALL also remain in `devDependencies` for local development.

REQ-097,REQ-097 — Assembler profiles produce separate PDFs per document,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The component descriptor SHALL define assembler profiles with dedicated nav files so that the assembler produces separate PDFs for requirements, architecture, and test-plan documents.

REQ-098,REQ-098 — Custom nav files select single documents,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""Each profile SHALL reference a custom nav file that contains a single xref to the target document, so only that page is included in the assembly.

REQ-099,REQ-099 — Single-PDF output is preserved,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The existing single-PDF configuration SHALL remain available via `antora-assembler-pdf.yml` and the existing `antora-playbook-pdf.yml` SHALL continue to produce a single merged PDF.

REQ-131,REQ-131 — DOCX wrapper script converts assembled AsciiDoc to DOCX,process_requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The project SHALL include an `adoc-to-docx` shell script that reads assembled AsciiDoc from stdin, converts it to DocBook using `asciidoctor -b docbook` with Kroki support, then pipes the result through `pandoc -f docbook -t docx` to produce a DOCX file.

REQ-132,REQ-132 — DOCX assembler configs mirror PDF assembler configs,process_requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""For each existing PDF assembler configuration, a corresponding DOCX assembler configuration SHALL exist that differs only in the build command, using `./adoc-to-docx` instead of `bundle exec asciidoctor-pdf`.

REQ-133,REQ-133 — PDF playbook includes DOCX assembler configurations,process_requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The `antora-playbook-pdf.yml` SHALL register DOCX assembler configs alongside PDF assembler configs so a single build produces both PDF and DOCX outputs.

REQ-134,REQ-134 — pandoc is available in the build environment,process_requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The project SHALL declare `pandoc` as a dependency in `devbox.json` so that `devbox shell` provides the pandoc binary for DOCX generation.

REQ-135,REQ-135 — DOCX output format is documented,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The project documentation SHALL include a how-to guide for generating DOCX output and reference documentation for the DOCX assembler configuration.

REQ-179,REQ-179 — PDF playbook references extension by local path in development,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The `antora-playbook-pdf.yml` example playbook SHALL reference the PDF extension using a local path (`./lib/src/antora-pdf-extension.cjs`) since it is the project's own development playbook.
Consumer documentation SHALL show the package subpath pattern (`antora-tracer/antora-pdf`).

REQ-180,REQ-180 — PDF extension is published and referenceable by package name,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The `antora-tracer` npm package SHALL include `lib/src/antora-pdf-extension.cjs` and export it under the subpath `antora-tracer/antora-pdf` so consumers can reference it in their playbooks without copying files from the repository.

REQ-181,REQ-181 — DOCX extension is published and referenceable by package name,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The `antora-tracer` npm package SHALL include `lib/src/antora-docx-extension.cjs` and `lib/src/antora-docx-converter.cjs` and export the extension under the subpath `antora-tracer/antora-docx`.

REQ-182,REQ-182 — Assembler packages declared as optional peer dependencies,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The `package.json` SHALL declare `@antora/assembler` and `@antora/pdf-extension` as `peerDependencies` with `optional: true` in `peerDependenciesMeta` so npm signals the requirement to consumers who use PDF or DOCX output without requiring them for consumers who do not.
These packages SHALL also remain in `devDependencies` for local development builds.

REQ-183,REQ-183 — Assembler configs and adoc-to-docx script are example-site configuration,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The assembler config YMLs and `adoc-to-docx` script SHALL reside in `examples/` as reference consumer configuration, not at the project root and not in the npm package.
The how-to documentation SHALL explain that consumers create their own configs modelled on these examples.

REQ-184,REQ-184 — DOCX playbook references extension by local path in development,process_requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The `antora-playbook-pdf.yml` example playbook SHALL reference the DOCX extension using a local path (`./lib/src/antora-docx-extension.cjs`).
Consumer documentation SHALL show the package subpath pattern (`antora-tracer/antora-docx`).

REQ-151,REQ-151 — Vale lints page and partial source content during the build,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL run Vale against the source AsciiDoc content of every page and partial file in the content catalog when the extension is enabled.

REQ-152,REQ-152 — The build gates on a configurable minimum severity,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL fail the build when Vale reports a finding at or above the configured minimum severity, and SHALL log findings below that severity without failing.

REQ-153,REQ-153 — The extension reports the Vale configuration source,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL load Vale's configuration from the path supplied in the playbook configuration, so users control which styles and rules apply.

REQ-154,REQ-154 — Missing executables fail with an actionable message,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""When the extension is enabled, if the `vale` or `asciidoctor` executable is unavailable, the system SHALL fail the build with a message naming the missing executable.

REQ-155,REQ-155 — The extension is opt-in,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL NOT run Vale unless the extension is explicitly registered in the playbook, so existing builds are unaffected.

REQ-156,REQ-156 — Source layout is out of scope,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL NOT enforce source line layout such as one sentence per line; that concern belongs to the source-layout checker.

REQ-157,REQ-157 — Reusable Vale rules encode the style guide,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL provide a set of Vale rule files that encode the machine-checkable parts of the documentation style guide, including filler-word avoidance, inclusive language, non-militaristic language, and the instead-of/use substitutions.

REQ-158,REQ-158 — Rules are packaged with the extension,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL ship the rule files and a sample configuration with the npm package, while remaining optional for users.
REQ-185,REQ-185 — Item blocks use the open-block delimiter,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""Item block examples in the documentation SHALL use the `--` open-block delimiter as the canonical form.
The `====` example-block delimiter SHALL be documented as a valid alternative with its rendering difference.

REQ-186,REQ-186 — Getting Started tutorial page,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The example site SHALL include a single Tutorial page (`getting-started.adoc`) that guides a first-time user from zero to a working traceability setup in numbered, sequential steps.

REQ-187,REQ-187 — Tutorial in navigation,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The example site navigation SHALL include a """"Tutorial"""" section as the first top-level item, containing the Getting Started page.
REQ-188,REQ-188 — How-to guide pages exist for key tasks,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The example site SHALL include How-to guide pages covering the following tasks:
* Contributing to the project (extracted from developer guide)

REQ-189,REQ-189 — How-to guides link to Reference,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""Each How-to guide page SHALL include links to relevant Reference pages for option details and syntax specifications.

REQ-190,REQ-190 — How-to guides section in navigation,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The example site navigation SHALL include a """"How-to Guides"""" section containing all how-to pages, ordered by typical usage frequency.

REQ-191,"""REQ-191 — Reference pages for macro syntax, configuration, CLI, presets, and API""",requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The example site SHALL include Reference pages exhaustively documenting:
* Traceability display macros (outgoing, incoming, links, graph, graph-coverage)
* Configuration options (all playbook options, traceability.yml schema)
* Public API surface (methods, signatures, data model interfaces)

REQ-192,REQ-192 — Reference pages cross-link to other modes,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""Reference pages SHALL include links to relevant How-to guides, Explanation pages, and other Reference pages.

REQ-193,REQ-193 — Reference section in navigation,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The example site navigation SHALL include a """"Reference"""" section containing all reference pages, ordered from most-used to least-used.
REQ-194,"""REQ-194 — Explanation pages for concepts, architecture, and design rationale""",requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The example site SHALL include Explanation pages covering:
* The traceability model (roles, relations, matrices as concepts)
* The processing pipeline (how passes work, the graph lifecycle)
* Antora vs Sphinx publishing pipeline comparison

REQ-195,REQ-195 — Explanation pages link to Reference and How-to,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""Explanation pages SHALL include links to relevant Reference pages and How-to guides for readers who want to act on the understanding gained.
REQ-196,REQ-196 — Explanation section in navigation,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The example site navigation SHALL include an """"Explanation"""" section containing all explanation pages.

REQ-197,REQ-197 — Self-Traceability nav section groups demo pages,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The example site navigation SHALL include a """"Self-Traceability"""" section containing the pages that demonstrate the extension tracing its own development artifacts:

REQ-198,REQ-198 — Self-Traceability section is visually distinct,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The Self-Traceability section SHALL be clearly separated from the user-facing documentation sections, signaling to readers that these are demonstration artifacts, not documentation about using the tool.
REQ-199,REQ-199 — Self-Traceability section preserves traceable items,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The restructuring SHALL NOT move any traceable `[item]` blocks out of their source files.
All existing requirements (REQ), architecture (ARC), test (TST), use case (UC), and quality (QA) items SHALL remain in their current AsciiDoc files.

REQ-218,REQ-218 — Design concepts address functional requirements,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""Every functional requirement (REQ) in the self-traceability example SHALL be addressed by at least one design concept (ARC item) via an `addresses:REQ-NNN[]` link.

REQ-200,REQ-200 — Doc examples validate against the traceability configuration,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL provide a check that extracts `[item]` blocks from the example site's prose documentation pages and validates them against the example traceability configuration (`examples/traceability.yml`).
The check SHALL fail on unknown roles, disallowed relations, and item blocks that fail to parse.

REQ-060,REQ-060 — Pages workflow generates PDFs,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The GitHub Pages workflow SHALL include Ruby setup and PDF generation steps so that requirements, architecture, and test-plan PDFs are built and deployed alongside the HTML site on every push to main.
REQ-061,REQ-061 — Site links to PDF downloads,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The example site's index page SHALL include download links to the three core PDF documents.

REQ-062,REQ-062 — Local PDF workflow is unchanged,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The existing local PDF build workflow (`devbox shell` + `npx antora antora-playbook-pdf.yml`) SHALL continue to work unchanged.

REQ-072,REQ-072 — Landing page at GitHub Pages root,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The system SHALL serve a landing page at the GitHub Pages root URL (`/`) that introduces the antora-tracer project before visitors enter the documentation, while the Antora documentation site remains accessible at `/docs/`.

REQ-073,REQ-073 — Two-persona feature presentation,requirement,,requirements.adoc,"""The landing page SHALL present project features in a way that resonates with both developers/architects (docs-as-code natives) and requirements engineers/project managers (traceability/compliance focused users).

ARC-001,ARC-001 — Project scope and architectural goals,design,,explanation/architecture.adoc,"""*Project scope and architectural goals*
The Antora Tracer is an Antora extension that adds role-based requirements traceability to AsciiDoc documentation.
It replaces fixed macro types with a single configurable `[item]` macro.
- Enable users to define their own traceability domain model (roles, relations, matrices) through YAML configuration
- Maintain a clean separation between parsing, graph storage, validation, matrix generation, and export
- Ship with built-in presets for common domains without requiring users to write configuration
- Integrate with Antora's event pipeline without imposing runtime dependencies on users who don't need specific features
- Provide a standalone CLI for use outside Antora

See the API reference for full signatures.

column1: The extension runs four passes inside `contentClassified`.
The sequence diagram above shows the Antora-level flow; this diagram focuses on the internal pass structure.

column3: What happens

column2: `processAsciiDocFile()` — DocumentParser extracts items + relationships, populates TraceabilityGraph. Both pages and partials are processed.

Graph must be complete before Pass 3 can resolve cross-file `addresses:TARGET[]` references. Both pages and partials are processed in all three passes — partial content is inlined into pages and reaches the browser.

`expandRelationMacros(file, macroName)` — replace `traceability:outgoing[]`, `traceability:incoming[]`, and `traceability:links[]` with formatted relationship lists (grouped by type, configurable style/order); macroName is `outgoing`, `incoming`, or `links`.
Depends on complete graph from Pass 1 to enumerate relationships. Opt-in via `:traceability-links:` document attribute; forced on for partials.

`expandGraphMacros()` + `expandCoverageMacros()` + `expandConfigGraphMacros()` — replace `traceability:graph[]`, `traceability:graph-coverage[]`, and `traceability:config-graph[]` with rendered diagram image references (DOT and Vega-Lite).
Uses `toDot()` / `toVegaLite()` / `toConfigDot()`. Opt-in via `:traceability-graph:` document attribute. Independent of Pass 2.
`substituteLinksInFile()` — replace inline relationship macros with `xref:page.html#ID` (pages) or `link:URL#ID` (partials). Also runs `injectTitleIds()` and `unindentItemMacros()`.
Needs complete graph (all sourceFiles known) from Pass 1. This is why Pass 1 processes all files before any macro expansion.

column1: - *Synchronous init*: `AntoraTraceabilityExtension` constructor initializes the traceability graph synchronously (config/preset loading is a synchronous file read) before any event handler is registered. This eliminates the race where a `contentClassified` event could fire before the graph is ready.
- *Single-pass processing*: `process()` call does both parsing and graph population in one call. No separate relationship processing pass needed.
- *Lazy rendering*: Templates are loaded and compiled on first use, cached thereafter.
The `prepareFile()` method computes file content, document attributes, and item block positions once per file, then feeds the same `PreparedFile` to all five macro-expansion methods.
This eliminates redundant buffer conversions and regex scans that were previously repeated in each method.

column2: Simplifies mental model, enables user-defined roles without code changes, reduces parser duplication

Role-based relation validation at processing time
Catches errors early, prevents invalid graphs, provides clear messages
No validation (allows invalid graphs), warning only (users miss issues), runtime validation (too late)
Separates presentation from logic, enables user customization, already working from prior work
Embedded HTML generation (code duplication), other template engines (Mustache was already in place)
Mature graph query capabilities, Cypher is industry standard, no need to build query language
Custom DSL (high effort), GraphQL (not graph-optimized), Gremlin (less popular)
Gives starting points, reduces config burden, demonstrates best practices

Forces explicit configuration, prevents domain model assumptions

Graceful degradation, partial config allowed, incremental role adoption
Error on unknown (too strict), silent ignore (users miss config issues)
Manual regex parsing over Asciidoctor.js extensions
Simpler, version-independent, easier to test, works consistently across Asciidoctor.js versions
Users define which roles go on rows and columns, which relations count as coverage
Hardcoded matrix types (req-impl, req-test, full) — inflexible for domain models with different roles
In-memory source substitution for clickable links

Tests `diffGraphs`: added/removed/unmodified classification, field-level modification reporting, suppression of removed items' relationships, relationship deltas on surviving items, and that a superseded pair appears as removed plus added with the `supersedes` link.

PRQ-001,PRQ-001 — CI workflows trigger on push and PR,process_requirement,,self-traceability/delivery-process.adoc,"""The GitHub Actions CI workflow SHALL trigger on every push to `main` and every pull request.
The workflow SHALL run on the latest Ubuntu runner and SHALL execute `npm ci`, `npm run build`, `npm test`, and `npm run lint` in sequence.
The CI pipeline ensures that every change is validated against the full test suite before it reaches users — no manual testing step required.

PRQ-002,PRQ-002 — Test suite runs as merge gate,process_requirement,,self-traceability/delivery-process.adoc,"""The test suite SHALL run as a required status check before merging any pull request to `main`.
The suite SHALL include 275+ tests covering the extension core, Antora integration, CLI, matrix generation, Neo4j export, and link substitution.
Any test failure SHALL block the merge.
PRQ-003,PRQ-003 — Example site builds without errors,process_requirement,,self-traceability/delivery-process.adoc,"""The example site SHALL build successfully as part of the CI pipeline.
The build SHALL include the Antora HTML site generation and PDF output.
Any xref warnings or build errors SHALL be treated as failures.
The site build exercises the full extension pipeline — parsing, macro expansion, link substitution, matrix generation, and matrix registration in the content catalog — serving as an integration test.

PRQ-004,PRQ-004 — Example site deploys from main branch,process_requirement,,self-traceability/delivery-process.adoc,"""The example site SHALL deploy to GitHub Pages automatically on every push to `main`.
The Pages workflow SHALL build the Antora site, generate PDFs, copy the landing page, and deploy to the `gh-pages` branch.
The deployment SHALL be atomic — either all artifacts deploy or none.
The deployed site serves as the project's public documentation and a live demonstration of the extension's capabilities.

PRQ-005,PRQ-005 — Release is tagged and versioned,process_requirement,,self-traceability/delivery-process.adoc,"""Every release SHALL be tagged with a semver tag (`v0.12.1`) and the version SHALL be updated in `package.json`.
The CHANGELOG SHALL be updated with all notable changes since the previous release.
The release SHALL be published to npm.
Versioning follows https://semver.org/[Semantic Versioning]: MAJOR for breaking API changes, MINOR for new features, PATCH for bug fixes and internal refactoring.

PRQ-006,PRQ-006 — PDF artifacts are generated alongside HTML,process_requirement,,self-traceability/delivery-process.adoc,"""The Pages workflow SHALL generate PDF artifacts for the requirements, architecture, and test-plan documents using `@antora/pdf-extension` with Ruby and `asciidoctor-pdf`.
PDFs SHALL be placed alongside HTML output in the deployed site.
The PDF pipeline is provisioned by `devbox.json` (Node.js + Ruby) and `Gemfile` (asciidoctor-pdf), ensuring reproducible builds across environments.
